profile.summary: RNABERT is a small RNA language model from Keio University that turns each base of a non-coding RNA sequence into a numerical vector (an embedding) that reflects its sequence context and secondary structure. It reads RNA sequences in FASTA format and outputs per-base embeddings, which the authors use to align RNAs by structure and to cluster them into RNA families.

summary_quotes.text: Department of Biosciences and Informatics, Keio University
we construct an informative base embedding method, RNABERT, for RNA sequences that takes into account the context and secondary structure of RNA sequences
RNABERT requires that RNA sequences be represented in fasta format.
To obtain the embedding vector for the RNA sequence, run
apply this algorithm to two fundamental RNA sequence problems: structural alignment and clustering

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each base gets a 120-dimensional token embedding plus a position embedding, and the sum passes through six Transformer layers. The output is a context-sensitive embedding for every base. Training alternates two tasks. In masked language modelling (MLM), some bases are hidden and predicted from the rest. In structural alignment learning (SAL), pairs of sequences from Rfam seed alignments are aligned using their embeddings, so that bases aligned in the reference alignment get similar embeddings. A structural alignment of two RNAs is then computed from the embeddings with the Needleman-Wunsch algorithm.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and methods, Figure 2 caption; Introduction; Discussion

quotes.text: Token and position embedding randomly generates a 120-dimensional vector representing four RNA bases. The transformer layer component consists of a stack of six transformer layers
The weights of the transformer layer are trained by alternately training two different tasks (MLM and SAL) on top of the output of the transformer layer.
The SAL task employs pre-training using seed alignments obtained from the Rfam database
so that the bases aligned in the seed structural alignment are expected to have more similar embeddings
the third procedure calculates the alignment by the Needleman–Wunsch algorithm

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pre-trained model file is offered, through a Google Drive link in the README, with no version number. The README says this model was trained on the full Rfam 14.3 dataset (about 400 nucleotides), while the paper describes MLM pre-training on 76 237 human small ncRNAs from RNAcentral and SAL training on Rfam alignments (TrainSet-A or TrainSet-B). Which of the paper's settings the download matches is not stated. A result should cite the repository commit and say that the Google Drive model was used.

strengths.text: The SAL task trains embeddings on Rfam structural alignments, so the embeddings are designed to carry secondary structure information, not sequence alone.

quotes.text: RNABERT introduces a novel pre-training task, SAL, in addition to the usual MLM task to more explicitly incorporate RNA secondary structure information into the base embedding for structural alignments.

strengths.text: The model is very small (six layers, 120-dimensional embeddings), and the repository includes training code and sample data for both pre-training tasks.

run_guide.summary: Install RNABERT, download the pre-trained model and write per-base embeddings for the repository's sample sequences.
prerequisites: Python 3.6.5 as used by the authors, PyTorch 1.4.0 or later, biopython 1.76 or later, and a C++17 compiler.
At least one NVIDIA GPU, as the README requires.
The pre-trained model file, downloaded by hand from the Google Drive link in the README. No licence is stated for it.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/mana438/RNABERT.git
cd RNABERT
git checkout --detach 1aeebcb2823bc34fc37f6527d63fca06917e3919
python setup.py install
steps.explanation: The README's clone line has the owner missing (https://github.com//RNABERT); the repository URL here is the one given in the paper. A checkout line is added to pin the commit read for this page.

steps.title: Write embeddings
steps.shell:
export PRED_FILE=sample/aln/sample.raw.fa
export PRE_WEIGHT=/path/to/pretrained/weight
export OUTPUT_FILE=/path/to/output/file

python MLM_SFP.py \
    --pretraining ${PRE_WEIGHT} \
    --data_embedding ${PRED_FILE} \
    --embedding_output ${OUTPUT_FILE} \
    --batch 40
steps.explanation: The README's embedding command, using the sample FASTA from its prediction section. Set PRE_WEIGHT to the downloaded model file and OUTPUT_FILE to the file to write; the README uses OUTPUT_FILE without defining it, so the export line is added. The README's version lacks a backslash after MLM_SFP.py and has a trailing one after --batch 40; both are corrected here so the command runs as one line.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The README's clone URL and line continuations are broken; the fixes made here are described in each step.
The software targets Python 3.6 and PyTorch 1.4 or later; newer environments were not checked.

notes: The repository has no licence file, so its README and config are hashed but not stored. MultiMolecule hosts an unofficial port of RNABERT on Hugging Face; it was not used. The record's area facet is dna-genomes, although RNABERT is an RNA model; consider rna-transcriptomes. The README and the paper disagree on the training data behind the downloadable model.
